answer: Copying the same citations across 292 aliases therefore forfeits the authoring cost 292 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the karst index resolves every citation against the ripple checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the beacon audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
